title: Portuguese capture of Malacca
summary: In 1511 a Portuguese force under Afonso de Albuquerque took Malacca, the port of the Malay sultanate on the Strait of Malacca. Sultan Mahmud Shah fled and the Portuguese raised the fortress A Famosa. It gave Portugal its first base in maritime Southeast Asia, and the exact day of the fall is given differently in different accounts.

uncertainty.note: Year is firm in all opened sources. The day is not fixed here: one popular history says Albuquerque had taken the city by 24 August; other accounts seen only in search snippets give 15 August or earlier July and August assaults. Only the year is claimed.

as_recorded.value: In 1511 the Portuguese led by Alfonso de Albequerque captured the city of Malacca.
By August 24, Albuquerque had taken the city.

where.historical_name: Malacca, capital of the Malacca Sultanate under Sultan Mahmud Shah

importance.justification: The first European seizure of a major Southeast Asian port-state, opening a colonial presence on the Strait of Malacca.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the day of capture (15 or 24 August; the opened pages give only the year or a late-August date from a popular site); the pin is the modern city centre, not the fortress. Britannica was not openable, so no scholarly source for the day was read.
